decisions_20260910.why_acceptable: These rows are DERIVED: they carry no authority, are never read as the source of truth for document content, permissions or ledger receipts, and are fully rebuilt from the source document's content by the next save (replace_knowledge_document_backlinks is an idempotent content-derived rebuild). No acknowledged write is lost, no ledger receipt is partial, no uniqueness or version invariant depends on them.
decisions_20260910.which_write_rebuilds_them: replace_knowledge_document_backlinks on the next save of the SOURCE document (api/knowledge_documents.rs save composition), or any explicit backlink rebuild.
decisions_20260910.blast_radius: A dangling derived row pointing at a tombstoned document until the source document is next saved. Visible in backlink panes and Loom edge counts; not visible in document content, versions, drafts, ledger receipts or search authority.
decisions_20260910.what_it_does_NOT_cover: It does NOT cover R1-1-2 (the delete transaction deciding backlink scope from a title-uniqueness read outside its write set, and stamping that decision into a durable tombstone). That is a correctness defect being FIXED in MT-142, not accepted: a durable receipt derived from an unconflictable read is authority, not derived data.
decisions_20260910.test_obligation: The swarm integrity oracle must not count this class as a lost write, but MUST assert the rebuild converges (save the source document and verify the derived rows agree) rather than ignoring the class (routed to Lane B).

defect_20260911_retry_budget.summary: guarded_mutation used RetryContext::unbounded(); RetryPolicy::CONTRACT.maximum_elapsed (2000 ms) bounds only SLEEPS (an in-flight attempt is deliberately never raced against the deadline so an acknowledged commit is never dropped); each attempt was bounded by statement_timeout (300 s) and maximum_attempts is 8. One contended mutation could therefore occupy 8 x 300 s = 40 minutes uninterruptibly. A2 s R1-1-2 remediation, which makes every title-mutating transaction write the title anchor, raised same-title contention and turned that latent bound into a real stall.

scope.summary: Prove and harden the SurrealDB-only storage layer for parallel model swarms. Exercise concurrent point reads, range/search queries, creates, idempotent upserts, optimistic updates, deletes and multi-record projection transactions against a real embedded SurrealDB RocksDB store. Measure conflicts, retries, retry exhaustion, lock wait, operation latency and throughput. Replace the coarse process-global RICH_DOCUMENT_MUTATION_LOCK and KNOWLEDGE_UPSERT_LOCK in storage/surreal/knowledge.rs with record/workspace-keyed contention control where local coordination is useful and with atomic Surreal transactions plus in-transaction guards where correctness must survive independent clients or future remote deployment. A keyed in-process lock is only a local contention-shaping optimization; it MUST NOT be the sole correctness mechanism for uniqueness, compare-and-set, versioning, idempotency, ledger/projection atomicity or lost-update prevention. Preserve SurrealDB as the only database: no PostgreSQL or SQLite driver, fallback, fixture, syntax, environment variable, server spawn or compatibility path may be introduced.

embedded_mode_boundary.supported_topology_to_prove: One embedded SurrealDB engine owns one RocksDB store path and is shared through cloned in-process database/client handles across parallel async tasks.
embedded_mode_boundary.forbidden_claim: Do not claim that multiple processes may open the same embedded RocksDB path concurrently. Do not use a second embedded engine on the same path as a distributed-concurrency test.
embedded_mode_boundary.future_remote_compatibility: All cross-client correctness invariants live in atomic SurrealQL transactions, conditional guards, stable record identities, version checks and idempotency keys. Tests must be able to use independent lock registries over the same database client/context so a process-local lock cannot masquerade as distributed correctness. A remote-server run may be added when a managed endpoint is configured, but an unconfigured remote run is reported as NOT_RUN_UNCONFIGURED and never as PASS.

contention_control_requirements: Eliminate RICH_DOCUMENT_MUTATION_LOCK and KNOWLEDGE_UPSERT_LOCK as coarse process-global serialization points.

Choose the narrowest verified stable key for local coordination: record identity for single-record mutations, normalized workspace-plus-natural-key for uniqueness/upsert races, and workspace identity only for invariants that genuinely span a workspace.
Cross-record operations use deterministic key ordering or one atomic Surreal transaction so nested acquisition cannot deadlock.
The keyed-lock registry has bounded or reclaimable cardinality; completed one-off record keys cannot leak lock entries indefinitely.
No read-only operation waits on an unrelated write lock. Disjoint-record and different-workspace writes must be observably concurrent.

Every invariant formerly protected only by a coarse mutex is revalidated inside the committing Surreal transaction. An independent-client proof must remain correct when the clients do not share a keyed-lock registry.

Inventory other process-global storage mutation locks under storage/surreal/. Retain singleton lifecycle/schema-bootstrap locks only with a written invariant; route product-data global locks to a follow-on MT or harden them in this MT when they share the same proven primitive and test surface.

retry_policy_requirements.algorithm: Bounded exponential backoff with full jitter and a caller-visible deadline/cancellation boundary.
retryable_only: Engine errors proven by pinned-version evidence to represent transient transaction/write conflict or temporary busy conditions
A transaction guard's explicitly typed retryable snapshot-change outcome when the complete operation is idempotent
never_retry: Validation, authorization, not-found, schema, corruption or invariant errors
Expected-version mismatch or stale caller state that requires the caller to merge or refresh
Unknown database errors without a pinned-version classification
Any operation without a stable idempotency key or otherwise proven replay safety
retry_policy_requirements.exhaustion_semantics: Return a typed retry-exhausted error preserving the final cause, attempts and elapsed time; emit the structured diagnostic exactly once; never spin, silently downgrade, fall back to another database or report success after an uncommitted write.
retry_policy_requirements.testability: Jitter randomness and time are injectable or seedable in tests so bounds, cancellation and exhaustion are deterministic without weakening production jitter.

ci_deterministic.workload: Mixed reads, searches, creates, idempotent upserts, optimistic versioned writes, deletes and multi-record projection/ledger transactions over same-record, disjoint-record, same-workspace and different-workspace keys.
ci_deterministic.hard_bound: Every worker and the whole test have explicit timeouts; a timeout is a failure, not an ignored test.

extended_local.workload: Seeded repeatable large-dataset run with configurable dataset size, read/write mix, key skew and contention ratio.
extended_local.gate: Run before READY_FOR_VALIDATION_V4 on the operator-designated machine. The report records machine context and selected numeric budgets; absolute cross-machine latency is not inferred from CI.

acceptance_criteria.text: A current pinned-version research basis is recorded before code changes and distinguishes SurrealDB transaction/isolation guarantees, embedded RocksDB single-owner constraints, retryable error classes and future remote-server behavior from assumptions.

RICH_DOCUMENT_MUTATION_LOCK and KNOWLEDGE_UPSERT_LOCK no longer exist as coarse global locks. Same-record and natural-key contention remains correct through atomic Surreal transactions and guards; disjoint records and different workspaces demonstrate at least two simultaneous in-flight writes rather than global serialization.

The deterministic CI profile runs at least 16 workers and 2,000 operations against a real embedded RocksDB store, covers reads, queries, creates, idempotent upserts, optimistic updates, deletes and multi-record transactions, and finishes with zero lost writes, zero duplicate natural keys/idempotency effects, zero partial projections or ledger receipts, zero dirty reads of uncommitted state, zero hangs and exact final counts/hashes.

Same-record tests prove explicit semantics: an expected-version race produces one committed winner and typed stale/conflict outcomes for losers; identical idempotency-key replays converge to one durable effect; disjoint-record operations all commit without unrelated lock waiting. No test accepts last-writer-wins where the API promises optimistic concurrency.

Retry behavior is bounded, jittered, cancellation-aware and limited to proven retryable/idempotent operations. Tests prove first-attempt success, eventual success after retryable conflicts, terminal-error no-retry, maximum-attempt exhaustion, maximum-elapsed exhaustion and cancellation, with no attempt beyond either configured bound.

The extended local profile runs at least 64 workers and 50,000 operations and emits a versioned machine-readable report containing workload seed/configuration, engine/SDK version, embedded/remote mode, dataset cardinality, attempted/succeeded/failed counts by operation, conflicts, conflict rate, retries, retry rate, retry exhaustion, lock-wait p50/p95/p99, operation-latency p50/p95/p99 by class, throughput, maximum concurrent operations, timeout/cancellation counts and final integrity verdict.

Lifecycle stress races reads and writes with graceful shutdown. Shutdown stops admission, drains or cancels in-flight work within an explicit bound, closes the one owning embedded engine without deadlock, then a real close-and-reopen proves every acknowledged write and no unacknowledged partial transaction is durable.

Correctness remains green for independent clients/SurrealDatabase wrappers that do not share a keyed-lock registry but do share the same owning database context. This proves local locks are optional contention control and database transactions/guards own future remote/distributed correctness.

A repo-wide and dependency scan proves no PostgreSQL or SQLite runtime, driver, fallback, fixture, syntax, environment variable or server-spawn path was introduced. SurrealDB remains the only database.

The keyed-lock registry's entry count returns to its documented idle bound after high-cardinality churn, and deterministic lock ordering plus timeout-backed tests prove no deadlock when multi-record operations overlap in opposite input order.

The built-in UserManual documents the embedded single-owner topology, safe parallel swarm use, retry/exhaustion behavior, how to run both load profiles, how a no-context model reads the structured report, and the distinction between current embedded proof and future configured remote proof.

Two independent adversarial reviewers using different lenses approve the final implementation after all blocker findings are remediated and re-reviewed: one concurrency-correctness/atomicity lens and one load/performance/lifecycle/operability lens.

risks: Replacing one global mutex with a per-record mutex can preserve throughput but still lose correctness across independent clients or a future remote deployment.
Retrying unknown, stale-version or non-idempotent failures can duplicate durable effects or hide a real invariant violation.
A keyed-lock registry can grow without bound under large-dataset/high-cardinality swarm traffic.
A load test can pass with zero meaningful contention, zero executed operations in one class, or globally serialized workers unless overlap and nonzero class counts are asserted.
An unbounded task, lock acquisition, database query, shutdown or reopen can hang the operator session.
Opening the same embedded RocksDB path from multiple processes can be mistaken for a supported distributed topology.
Readers can observe mismatched document, projection, backlink or EventLedger state if multi-record writes stop being atomic.
Absolute latency thresholds can create false confidence across machines unless workload, engine version and machine context are recorded.
minimum_controls: Database transactions/guards and idempotency own correctness; local keyed locks are optional optimization only.
Every task, lock wait, query, retry loop, shutdown and reopen proof is explicitly bounded.
Every required workload class asserts a nonzero executed count and final canonical-state reconciliation.
Same-key, disjoint-key, same-workspace, different-workspace and independent-client scenarios are all mandatory.
Retry tests inject every classified outcome and prove exact attempt/elapsed bounds.
Lock-registry cardinality and reclamation are measured after high-cardinality churn.
No remote or distributed PASS is emitted without a configured real remote endpoint; embedded same-path multi-process access is forbidden.

Two independent adversarial reviews are required after implementation and after each blocker remediation, with one reviewer focused on concurrency correctness/atomicity and the other on load/performance/lifecycle/operability.
